problems.label: Recurring low periods with shorter high-energy spells
definitions: Has repeated weeks of low mood, low energy and loss of interest that make work and home life hard.
Describes short spells of unusual energy, confidence and less need for sleep that others noticed.
Has tried treatments for low mood that did not help or that seemed to set off a high.
longTermGoals: Low periods become less frequent and less severe, and highs are spotted early, so the client can keep their roles and relationships steady.

shortTermObjectives.text: Within 2 weeks, attend a psychiatric evaluation and share the history of highs as well as lows.
By session 4, list at least 3 early signs of a low and 3 of a high, with one first step for each.
For 4 weeks, track sleep, routine anchors and mood daily, and choose 2 anchors to make more regular.
During low periods, schedule and complete at least 3 small valued activities a week, rating mood before and after.
By session 2, complete a written safety plan with warning signs, coping steps, people and services to contact, and steps to make the home safer, and review it at least monthly.
Complete the PHQ-9 at intake and every 2 to 4 weeks; review the trend with the prescriber at each visit.

problems.label: Early warning signs, sleep changes and family stress around mood episodes
definitions: Past episodes followed changes in sleep, routine or stress that were noticed late.
Conflict at home rises around mood changes, and family members are unsure how to help.
longTermGoals: Early signs are noticed and acted on quickly with an agreed plan, and family life is calmer and more supportive.

shortTermObjectives.text: By session 6, write the client's personal list of early signs of a high and of a low (for example sleeping less, more spending or pulling back from people), with a matching action and contact for each.
For 8 weeks, record mood, hours of sleep and daily routine anchors each day, and look at the record together at each session to catch changes early.
When the record shows 2 nights in a row of much less sleep than usual, follow the agreed sleep-protection steps and contact the prescriber or clinician the same week.
With consent, take part in family-focused sessions with a trained clinician over 3 to 9 months (information about the condition, communication practice and problem solving together).

collaborativeNote: Write goals and objectives with the client in their own words. Timelines and targets are examples to adapt; the client decides what matters, and the clinician checks safety and fit.
